q: The alkanes are the simplest family of organic compounds and are referred to as the "_____ hydrocarbons".
e: The alkanes are the simplest family of organic compounds and are referred to as the "saturated hydrocarbons". An organic compound has carbon and hydrogen with at least one C-C or C-H covalent bond. Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with only single bonds and the general formula CnH2n+2. Hydrocarbons contain only carbon and hydrogen, joined by covalent bonds.

q: Every carbon in an alkane has a _____ environment and is bonded to four other atoms.
e: Every carbon in an alkane has a tetrahedral environment and is bonded to four other atoms. Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with only single bonds and the general formula CnH2n+2. Tetrahedral is the word this version is asking about.

q: Alkanes form a homologous series with the general formula _____.
e: Alkanes form a homologous series with the general formula C_nH2n+2. Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with only single bonds and the general formula CnH2n+2. A homologous series is a family of compounds with the same functional group and a general formula that rises by CH2. A general formula such as CnH2n+2 describes a whole homologous series at once.

q: In the IUPAC nomenclature system, the root name for an organic compound indicates the number of carbon atoms in the _____ continuous chain of carbon atoms.
e: In the IUPAC nomenclature system, the root name for an organic compound indicates the number of carbon atoms in the longest continuous chain of carbon atoms. An organic compound has carbon and hydrogen with at least one C-C or C-H covalent bond.

q: When naming alkanes, the C atoms in the longest chain are numbered beginning at the end nearest the _____.

q: Two or more compounds with the same molecular formula but different arrangements of atoms and have different properties from each other are called _____.
e: Two or more compounds with the same molecular formula but different arrangements of atoms and have different properties from each other are called isomers. Isomers share a molecular formula but differ in how the atoms are arranged, so their properties differ. The molecular formula gives the actual number of each kind of atom in one molecule. Isomers is the word this version is asking about.

q: Straight chain and branched-chain isomers are examples of _____ isomers.
e: Straight chain and branched-chain isomers are examples of structural isomers. Isomers share a molecular formula but differ in how the atoms are arranged, so their properties differ.

q: All of the alkanes containing _____ or more carbon atoms show structural isomerism.

Isomers share a molecular formula but differ in how the atoms are arranged, so their properties differ. Four is the word this version is asking about.

q: The reduction of alkyl halides with molecular hydrogen takes place in the presence of a catalyst like platinum or _____.
e: The reduction of alkyl halides with molecular hydrogen takes place in the presence of a catalyst like platinum or palladium. A catalyst speeds a reaction by lowering activation energy and is not used up in the overall change.

q: The normal alkanes from $C_1$ to $C_4$ are colourless _____.

q: The most important chemical reactions of saturated hydrocarbons are the substitution and _____ reactions.
e: The most important chemical reactions of saturated hydrocarbons are the substitution and combustion reactions. Hydrocarbons contain only carbon and hydrogen, joined by covalent bonds. Saturated hydrocarbons contain only single bonds between carbon atoms.

q: When methane is mixed with chlorine in diffused sunlight, a _____ reaction occurs where one chlorine atom replaces one hydrogen atom in each step.
e: When methane is mixed with chlorine in diffused sunlight, a substitution reaction occurs where one chlorine atom replaces one hydrogen atom in each step. In a substitution reaction one atom or group on carbon is replaced by another.

q: If there is not enough oxygen, alkanes undergo incomplete combustion, giving off poisonous _____ and less heat energy.

q: The reduction of alkenes is also known as _____.
